transcript: Last night I went to see A simulacrum at Atlantic Theater Company, a new play created by Lucas Nath and Steve Chiffo. Steve is a magician, and in this play we see a recreation of some of the workshops Steve and Lucas had together to create this piece. Much of the show is Steve presenting various magic tricks and speaking with Lucas, who's heard through a tape recorder. On stage, the two of them interrogate magic as an art form and Steve's relationship to it. Dramatizing a situation where we look behind the curtain of magic, which is an art form where presentation is a large part of it, is a really interesting dynamic. Lucas also poses some interesting questions about Steve's identity as an artist in relation to magic routines that are in many ways recreations of other magic routines. Now, I didn't think this piece went as deep as I hoped it would, but Steve was very compelling to watch, and I was really impressed by the magic. And I'd also give a lot of credit to the fact that this piece is very original with that. Another program for my collection.
